meta.notes: DRAFT, design-shape data (design/ORISON_DIALOGUE_DRAFTS_2026-10-22.md). Threshold conversation; no case, no resolution flags (Bible IV.1). Evelyn notices the lesson plan, the corrected list, the timetable, a child's mistake remembered decades later. Lucid demonstrations, leading questions, correction delivered as care; anger becomes impeccable grammar. Comic engine: praise so specifically conditional it reveals the trap. Never impressed by disorder. One name in her register is upstairs in 4A; she corrects Peter at the mail bank most evenings and neither names it.

em_open.line: You may come in. Wipe your feet; I shan't say it again, which is a thing I used to say and then say again. The papers on the table have graded themselves overnight. Red pencil. Not my hand. Very nearly my hand. I would like you to look at the marking and tell me what is wrong with it.

choices.label: It's too harsh.
It's accurate. That's what's wrong with it.
The spare cup. Never used. [the guest cup]
choices.evidence: a spare guest cup, never once used

em_sil1.line: You are reading before you answer. Good. I had a boy once who read before he answered and I corrected him for slowness, and he took it to heart, and I have never forgiven myself for being obeyed.

choices.label: It's accurate. That's what's wrong with it.

em_harsh.line: It is not harsh. Every mark is correct. 'Harsh' is what people say when a correction is accurate and they wish it were not. Try again, and this time read the page.

choices.label: It's accurate. That's what's wrong with it.

em_cup.line: For a guest. I set two every morning in case. Thirty years of in case. It has never had tea in it and it is the cleanest thing I own. ... You are not to read anything into a cup. It is a cup. I have corrected children for less.

choices.label: You set it for someone in particular.
It's accurate. That's what's wrong with it.

em_particular.line: I set it for whoever comes. Nobody comes; that is a fact about the building and not about the cup. ... There is a boy. He is not a boy. He lives upstairs and I meet him at the letter boxes and I correct one small thing and he thanks me, and neither of us has ever come up the other's stair. Sit down. I did not mean to say that.

choices.label: It's accurate. That's what's wrong with it.

em_accurate.line: Yes. Every mark is right and every page is covered in them, and a page that is all correction is not a corrected page, it is a red page. I know that now. I taught forty years before I knew it. The pencil on the table does not know it yet; it is only doing what I did.

choices.label: Then it's not grading the papers. It's grading you.
Which page did it grade hardest?
You were a good teacher.

em_accurate_sil.line: You have let the sentence stand without improving it. I notice that. I am not sure I could.

choices.label: Which page did it grade hardest?

em_good_teacher.line: I was an excellent teacher. Excellence is not the question. Kindness is the question, and I have been marking my own answer to it in red for a very long time. Do not praise me; I can hear the conditions in it. I invented them.

choices.label: Which page did it grade hardest?

em_grading_you.line: ... The grocery list. The letter to my sister I never posted. My own hand, on my own table, every line of it corrected by a hand very nearly mine. Yes. It is grading me. It has given me what I gave, and I find I do not want it, and I find I have no grounds to refuse.

choices.label: Which page did it grade hardest?

em_hardest.line: The register. The old one, from the year I taught the class I think about. It has gone through every name and marked one of them. One. A boy who was careful. I filled his margins until careful became frightened, and he thanked me for it, and he is upstairs, and the register has drawn a red line under his name as if to say: this one. This is the one you did.

choices.label: He keeps a note from you. Red ink. 'See me.'
Go up and tell him good enough can hold.
You can't blame yourself for a careful child.

em_hardest_sil.line: You have not told me what I ought to feel. Everyone tells me what I ought to feel; it is the one correction I cannot accept and the one I most deserve. Thank you for leaving the margin empty.

choices.label: Go up and tell him good enough can hold.

em_blame.line: I do not blame myself. Blame is a child's word. I am responsible, which is an adult's, and the difference is that responsibility can go upstairs. Blame only sits in a chair.

choices.label: Then go up.

em_see_me.line: ... He kept it. 'See me.' I wrote that on a good composition because it had one comma wrong, and I wanted him to come to the desk so I could tell him it was good, and he came to the desk and I told him about the comma. Forty years. He has carried the comma. I shall need to sit.

choices.label: Go up and tell him good enough can hold.

em_go_up.line: Good enough. ... I wrote that on the ones I had given up on. He will have read it as a verdict; I taught him to. If I go up I shall have to say it as a kindness, and I am not certain my mouth knows the shape. ... Put the kettle on. Both cups. I shall practise on you.

em_rt_open.line: You have come at a convenient hour, which I appreciate more than you know. The papers have stopped. I have not. I have been baking for people who did not ask; it is the same reflex in a kinder flour.

choices.label: You taught Peter. He's in 4A.
You tidy the noticeboard. Red pencil on the notices.
Teresa knocks on your door before her shift.

em_rt_sil.line: No question? Then you shall have tea for not asking one, which is the first time I have rewarded that.

choices.label: You tidy the noticeboard. Red pencil on the notices.

em_notices.line: Somebody must. Management's commas are a disgrace. ... I know. I know what it looks like, a woman correcting the landlord's grammar in a lobby. It is the only desk I have left and I am using it badly.

em_peter.line: I meet him at the boxes. I correct one thing. He says thank you and goes up with his post held like a verdict. Forty years and I have never once said his name there; if I said it he would know I know, and then one of us would have to climb a stair. I have decided it will be me. I have not decided when.

em_teresa.line: The nurse. One knock, before her shift, to see if I answer. I always answer. She has never once come in and I have never once asked her to; it is the most sensible arrangement in the building and I think it is also the loneliest, and I cannot work out which of us it is lonely for.

em_int_open.line: I wrote 'good enough' on a list this morning. My own. I have not corrected it.

choices.label: [Leave the list alone.]

em_fb_open.line: The pencil has started on the wallpaper. It is right about the wallpaper.

choices.label: I'll come back when it's stopped.

em_fb_sil.line: Mind the step. I have told Management about the step. In writing. Twice.

em_res_open.line: I went up. I said it. He said 'is that an instruction,' and I said yes, and he wrote it down. Two cups, this morning. One of them had tea in it.
